mechanism: Erythromycin is a CYP3A4 inhibitor that reduces cenobamate metabolism, increasing cenobamate plasma concentrations and risk of toxicity; cenobamate also induces CYP3A4 which may reduce erythromycin efficacy.
action: Monitor closely for cenobamate toxicity (dizziness, ataxia, diplopia); consider alternative macrolide or reduce cenobamate dose; avoid combination if possible due to bidirectional interaction.
